proposals.evidence: DEDR196(a) explicitly gives Kota ayṇ father, with Toda in/eyī (vocative eyā) and Tamil ayyan. LSI eyan Father and Of a Father preserve the father stem in separate elicitation slots, with vowel/nasal transcription differences. No unprinted genitive suffix is supplied and the original case gloss is retained; the article also notes a questioned Indo-Aryan comparison.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4395(a) and4616 both explicitly cite Kota pe-mog woman, providing the female + child/person analysis of LSI pemmage. The survey has medial mm, a and final e rather than the dictionary spelling; these are retained. In4395 the Badaga borrowing annotation belongs specifically to eṇ, not to the separate peṇ or pe- entries.
